title: A1-11 · Numbers from 0 a 10; Arabic and Indo-Arabic figures

blocks.text: A1-11 · Numbers from 0 a 10; Arabic and Indo-Arabic figures
Lesson overview

Phone numbers, document numbers, plates, hotel rooms, age: the numbers appear in every practical exchange. The figures you know from L0-10; Now learn to tell them and write them in letters. In this unit you actively use numbers from 0 a 10 "by itself', i.e. by counting and dictating figures; the dozens and composite numbers you learn to say age and to recognize them. The agreement of the number with the numbered name, which in Arabic has its own rules, you will see it in A2: here you just need the rule of ⁧كَمْ⁩ ( A1-06).

rows: 6–7 hours · one week (week 29 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-11), voice synthesis script, your document with numbers (patent, card) to practice
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. say, read and write in letters the numbers from 0 a 10;
2. Moving from European figures to Indo-Arabs and vice versa;
3. to dictate and understand telephone, document and plate numbers, digit by digit;
4. Recognize numbers from 11 a 100 and the dozens;
5. tell your age and understand the age stated by others;
6. fill in the numerical fields of a form.

2. Numbers from 0 a 10
10 ⁧عَشَرَة١٠⁩ ʿašara

Why they end up in ⁧ة⁩ . When you count (- one, two, three...) you use the shape with ⁧ة⁩ from 3 a 10. It is the basic form of the number. In front of a name the number changes ( ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ⁩ • three books • ⁧ثَلَاثُ سَيَّارَاتٍ⁩ • three cars: this is the rule of the agreement • on the contrary • that you will study in A2. For now, recognize her. ⁧وَاحِد⁩ and ⁧اِثْنَان⁩ have also the female: ⁧وَاحِدَة⁩ , ⁧اِثْنَتَان⁩ . They follow the name as adjectives: ⁧بِنْتٌ وَاحِدَةٌ⁩ One daughter is only one daughter.A1-09). ⁧صِفْر⁩ He gave English the word "cifra" and, through medieval Latin, "zero." The numbers. The direction is always from left to right, even in an Arabic line (L0-10). The ⁧٥⁩ ( 5) is a small circle; The zero ⁧٠⁩ It's a point. In handwriting 2 and 3 They look alike: ⁧٢⁩ has only one tooth at the top, ⁧٣⁩ Two. In texts without vowels the number is almost always written in digits; in letters only in legal texts, checks and formal documents.
3. Phone, documents, plates

rows: What's your phone number? (to a woman)

blocks.text: How they dictate. Encrypt by digit, with the number alone paused: ṣifr, iṯnān, wāḥid… . Those who say often repeat the number twice; The writer reads it again: it is the safest practice in any language. The letters in the numbers. Passports and plates may contain letters. Egyptian plates, for example, have Arabic letters and Indo-Arabic digits: the part in letters reads from right to left, the part in digits from left to right. The letters are read by their name: ⁧ب⁩ bāʾ , ⁧س⁩ sīn . The Latin letters of passports are usually read by the English or French name of the letter, which varies from country to country: in case of doubt, they are written. In Egypt the national identity number is called ⁧الرَّقْمُ القَوْمِيُّ⁩ ar-raqmu l-qawmī ; in other countries ⁧رَقْمُ الهُوِيَّةِ⁩ . You'll recognize both formulas in the forms.
4. From 11 a 100: recognize

How they form. From 13 a 19: unit + ⁧عَشَرَ⁩ , all with vowel -a, no variations. The dozens are the units with -ūna (in genitive and accusative) -īna, A1-19): ⁧ثَلَاثُونَ⁩ , ⁧أَرْبَعُونَ⁩ ; 20 It's irregular. From 21 a 99 Arabic first says units, then tens, joined by ⁧وَ⁩ : ⁧خَمْسَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ⁩ Five and twenty, as in German. The figure is written from left to right: . ⁧٢٥ مِائَة⁩ It's written with an alif that doesn't say: miʾa . It is a traditional spelling; the graph ⁧مِئَة⁩ It's more modern. You recognize both of them.

6. Dialogue 2 · At the hotel
Laylā arrives at a hotel in Milan.

Good evening. Do you have a reservation?
Laylā: Yes. On behalf Laylā Ḥaddād.

blocks.text: ⁧غُرْفَتُكِ رَقْمُ⁩ . ⁧شُكْرًا⁩ : ⁧المُوَظَّفُ⁩ al-muwaẓẓaf: šukran. ġurfatuki raqmu The clerk: Thank you. His room is the . ⁧عَشَرَة، وَهٰذَا المِفْتَاحُ⁩ ʿašara, wa-hāḏā l-miftāḥ. Number ten, and here's the key.

al-muwaẓẓaf: naʿam, fī ṭ-ṭābiqi l-awwal. wa-raqmu l-istiqbāli tisʿa.
The clerk: Yes, on the first floor. And the front desk number is nine.

blocks.text: What to notice. ⁧غُرْفَتُكِ رَقْمُ عَشَرَة⁩ Your room [is] number ten: after ⁧رَقْمُ⁩ the number is said in form to count and usually without desinence. The clerk gives of the "tu" (-ki) as is normal in MSA.
7. Pronunciation

⁧ث⁩ in ⁧ثَلَاثَة⁩ , ⁧ثَمَانِيَة⁩ . Deaf Interdental [θ], twice in ⁧ثَلَاثَة⁩ : ṯalāṯa . The most frequent error is t-talata; "Salasa" is the pronunciation of many dialects, not to be imitated. ⁧ع⁩ in ⁧أَرْبَعَة⁩ , ⁧سَبْعَة⁩ , ⁧تِسْعَة⁩ , ⁧عَشَرَة⁩ . Four out of ten numbers contain ʿayn. Fast dictation is the first thing you lose: keep it. The šadda of ⁧سِتَّة⁩ . sitta , with double t; the dozens: ⁧سِتُّونَ⁩ sittūn . . ⁧خَمْسَة⁩ ḫāʾ initial scraping; Don't confuse her with h. . ⁧صِفْر⁩ ṣād emphasis: the i sounds darker, almost [and].
8. New lexicon
⁧مِيلَاد⁩ mīlād birth ⁧و ل د⁩ name m.

Notes of use. ⁧عَام⁩ and ⁧سَنَة⁩ both mean "year': ⁧سَنَة⁩ is more common in speech and age, ⁧عَام⁩ in the press. ⁧تَارِيخ⁩ it means both "data" and "history" (the discipline). ⁧أَلْف⁩ plural ⁧آلَاف⁩ : ⁧آلَافُ اللَّاجِئِينَ⁩ Thousands of refugees are frequently reported.
